prompts.text: What's a theatrical tradition you would like to understand through seeing it performed in its original setting?
Tell me about watching a performance where the audience seemed to know when and how to respond.
A cultural centre is presenting a traditional drama to newcomers. What context should it provide before the show begins?
Theatre traditions can preserve a community's humour and concerns even as the stories evolve.
Learning how traditional masks are used in performance or studying how storytelling and music work together onstage?
The relationship between performers and spectators can be an essential part of a theatrical tradition.
Have you noticed how a familiar story changes when performed with different gestures or costumes?
A troupe wants to adapt an old play for younger audiences. Which elements would you ask them to consider carefully?
Describe a performance that made you curious about the history of the community that created it.
How can audiences appreciate unfamiliar performance traditions without expecting them to follow the conventions of modern film or theatre?
What's a proverb you heard growing up whose meaning became clearer only with experience?
Tell me about someone using a traditional saying to explain an ordinary disagreement.
A visitor hears a proverb translated word for word and finds it confusing. How could you explain the situation where it's usually used?
A good proverb can invite thought without always telling people exactly what to do.
Learning the stories behind animal proverbs or comparing sayings about patience across cultures?
Some sayings remain memorable because their images are funny even when the lesson is serious.
Have you discovered two very different proverbs that express a surprisingly similar idea?
A teacher wants children to explore proverbs without simply memorising them. What activity might help?
Describe hearing a familiar saying used in an unexpected context that made everyone laugh.
How do proverbs evolve when younger generations apply them to new situations?
What everyday design detail makes you immediately think of a particular place or cultural tradition?
Tell me about seeing a modern object that subtly borrowed a traditional craft technique.
A designer wants to collaborate with a community whose visual traditions they admire. What should the first conversation cover?
Cultural inspiration becomes more meaningful when creators acknowledge the people and stories behind it.
Exploring traditional typography and lettering or studying patterns used in woven materials?
A familiar symbol can look different when translated from cloth to print or digital screens.
Have you noticed how local materials shape the way designers approach furniture or household objects?
A public library wants a new visual identity rooted in the neighbourhood. Whose perspectives would you seek?
Describe finding a design that brought together older methods and newer needs particularly well.
What makes a design feel connected to a place without relying on the most obvious cultural symbols?
What's a traditional calendar or seasonal cycle that you would like to understand more deeply?
Tell me about discovering why a community observes an event at a different time from another.
You are explaining a lunar calendar to someone used only to fixed months. What everyday example might help?
Calendars reveal how communities have organised work, seasons and celebrations over long periods.
Learning how harvest seasons shaped a festival calendar or exploring traditional ways of marking the start of a new year?
A calendar can encode local environmental knowledge as well as a way of counting days.
Have you noticed how different communities mark the transition from one stage of life or year to another?
A museum wants visitors to understand several calendar systems without presenting one as the default. How might it organise the exhibit?
Describe a holiday whose date or timing made more sense after somebody explained its history.
How do people balance official calendars with traditional cycles that remain important to their community?
What useful knowledge about plants, weather or landscapes is passed down informally where you grew up?
Tell me about somebody explaining how they recognise a change in season without checking a forecast.
A community plans to document older residents' observations about local rivers or trees. What questions should researchers ask?
Traditional environmental knowledge deserves careful attention to its local context rather than romanticising or dismissing it.
Learning how craftspeople choose locally available wood or understanding traditional ways of conserving water?
People who work closely with land and seasons often notice subtle changes others overlook.
Have you learned something practical about nature from someone outside a classroom?
An environmental project wants to combine scientific measurements with residents' long-term observations. How could both contribute?
Describe a local environmental practice whose reason you understood only after asking about it.
How can traditional knowledge be documented while respecting the people who developed and maintain it?
What makes travelling on public transport feel distinctly different from one city to another?
Tell me about noticing a local travel custom when you first used buses, trains or ferries in a new place.
A visitor needs to understand the unwritten rules of your city's transport. What would you explain first?
Public transport has its own little social conventions that rarely appear on official maps.
Exploring the history of colourful buses or learning how communal taxis became part of city life?
The calls of conductors, conversations and route names can become part of a city's cultural soundscape.
Have you ever noticed passengers helping one another navigate a system through shared informal knowledge?
A museum is documenting transport culture. What ordinary objects or stories should it preserve?
Describe a journey where a familiar transport custom became a conversation starter.
How can cities modernise transport while preserving the community connections people have built around it?
What milestone does your community mark in a way that people elsewhere might not expect?
Tell me about attending a coming-of-age, graduation or other life-transition ceremony that taught you something.
You're invited to a ceremony you don't know well. What would you ask about the roles of guests and participants?
Milestone ceremonies often express what a community hopes for a person rather than simply marking their age.
Learning about traditional naming celebrations or understanding customs around apprentices finishing their training?
A public ritual can make a personal transition feel shared across several generations.
Have you seen a family adapt a milestone celebration to better reflect its present circumstances?
A young person wants to understand the meaning of a traditional ceremony before joining. Who might offer a thoughtful explanation?
Describe an occasion where a short speech or gesture made a familiar milestone feel significant.
How do communities decide which ceremonies should be optional, private or open to visitors?
What could an old local newspaper teach us about everyday concerns that history books rarely mention?
Tell me about reading an old advertisement or community notice that made you smile at how life had changed.
You can spend one afternoon in a small-town newspaper archive. What kind of story would you search for?
Local journalism can preserve details of community life long after larger events dominate people's memories.
Comparing old cultural event listings or reading letters to the editor from several generations ago?
Small announcements about markets, performances and schools often reveal how a community spent its time.
Have you ever seen a local story that deserved wider attention but never reached national news?
A community magazine wants to record changing traditions. Whose voices would you invite to contribute?
Describe discovering something about your area through an old printed source rather than someone's memory.
How can local media preserve cultural differences without treating people as curiosities?
What's a local building or craft material whose use you would like to understand better?
Tell me about seeing someone transform a very ordinary natural material into a remarkable object.
A maker gives you clay, reeds and wood from their region. What would you ask before attempting a design?
The materials available in a place can shape its creative traditions as strongly as people's artistic preferences.
Learning how natural dyes are made or discovering how locally sourced fibres are prepared for weaving?
Two regions may develop different craft styles partly because their climates and raw materials differ.
Have you noticed how the texture of a traditional material changes the way a finished object looks and feels?
A craft workshop wants to substitute an imported material with a local one. What qualities would they need to test?
Describe learning why an artisan preferred a traditional material even when a modern alternative was available.
What questions could reveal the environmental and cultural costs of producing a handmade object?
How do you think cultural traditions change when a community has to rebuild after a major disruption?
Tell me about a community event that returned after being absent for several years and what that meant to people.
A local cultural centre has lost part of its archive. How could residents help reconstruct the stories it held?
Keeping a tradition alive may sometimes require changing how it is practised.
Recording older residents' memories of a festival or helping younger makers relearn a nearly forgotten craft?
Communities can carry cultural memory through people even when familiar buildings or objects disappear.
What would make you hopeful about a cultural practice that only a few people still know how to perform?
A town wants to revive a community gathering but no longer has the old venue. What could guide a respectful new format?
Describe witnessing people preserve an important shared experience by adapting to new circumstances.
Who should have the strongest voice when a cultural practice is being revived or reinterpreted?
